L9: # Title:Local-to-global maximality for plurisubharmonic functions with locally analytic singularities
L10: 
L11: Authors:【6†Thai Duong Do】, 【7†Pham Hoang Hiep】
L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled Local-to-global maximality for plurisubharmonic functions with locally analytic singularities, by Thai Duong Do and Pham Hoang Hiep
L14: 
L15: 【8†View PDF】 【9†HTML (experimental)】
L16: > Abstract:We prove that a locally maximal plurisubharmonic function on a domain in $\bC^n$, $n\geq2$, is maximal if it has locally analytic singularities with a two-sided locally bounded remainder. Using McAdam's theorem, we show that local maximality forces the analytic spread of each defining ideal to be less than $n$. We use normalized blow-ups and Siu's analyticity theorem to compare singularities through generic divisorial Lelong numbers.
L17: We also obtain a criterion for maximality in terms of maximality outside the pole set and the analytic spread of the local defining ideals.

L9: # Title:Comparison principles for local plurisubharmonic potentials on complex manifolds and applications
L10: 
L11: Authors:【6†Thai Duong Do】, 【7†Pham Hoang Hiep】
L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled Comparison principles for local plurisubharmonic potentials on complex manifolds and applications, by Thai Duong Do and Pham Hoang Hiep
L14: 
L15: 【8†View PDF】 【9†HTML (experimental)】
L16: > Abstract:We prove a weighted comparison principle for local plurisubharmonic potentials in Cegrell's class on an arbitrary complex manifold under suitable boundary and gluing conditions. We obtain domination and uniqueness when the manifold admits a global psh function in $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}$ whose Monge-Ampère measure has an absolutely continuous part with positive density almost everywhere.
L17: We apply these results to plurisubharmonic functions on domains in $\mathbb C^2$ whose singularities satisfy local inequalities involving $\alpha\log\|f\|$ and a Cegrell potential. For such functions, maximality is equivalent to the vanishing of the Monge-Ampère measure of the current remaining after subtraction of the Siu divisorial part. Consequently, maximality is a local property in this class.

L9: # Title:Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions and Fujii-Seo Determinants in Hilbert spaces
L10: 
L11: Authors:【6†Per Åhag】, 【7†Rafał Czyż】, 【8†Antti Perälä】, 【9†Jani Virtanen】
L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions and Fujii-Seo Determinants in Hilbert spaces, by Per {\AA}hag and 3 other authors
L14: 
L15: 【10†View PDF】 【11†HTML (experimental)】
L16: > Abstract:A maximal plurisubharmonic function on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space can have an injective, noncompact Levi operator at every point. This raises the question of what replaces the finite-dimensional determinant criterion for maximality. We prove that a twice continuously differentiable plurisubharmonic function is maximal if its Levi operator is compact at every point, without any boundedness assumption on the function.
L17: Using the normalized determinants of Fujii and Seo, we also characterize local maximality by the condition that the infimum of the spectrum of the Levi operator is zero. The same condition characterizes maximality when the function is bounded on the closure of every bounded open set whose closure lies in the domain. The compactness result follows from a more general spectral criterion.
L18: Its proof combines a bounded transformation with the smooth variational principle of Borwein and Preiss to establish comparison on bounded open sets whose closures need not be compact.
